name: Mistral AI
desc: French developer of open and commercial large language models, the Vibe assistant and enterprise AI deployments.
capacity_detail: Equity rounds include EUR 1.7B (Sep 2025) and EUR 3.0B Series D (Sep 2026); earlier EUR 600M (Jun 2024)
markets: Headquartered in Paris with datacentres planned in France and Sweden; partners include Microsoft, NVIDIA, Accenture and CMA CGM.

signals.raise: EUR 3B round with Samsung Electronics taking a stake (Sep 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_AI)
signals.marketing: Le Chat assistant renamed Vibe (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_AI)

rationale: Europe's flagship AI lab competing with Anthropic and OpenAI; F1 could build a global consumer brand for Vibe and enterprise credibility.

name: Poolside
desc: Builds foundation models and agents for software development, offered to enterprises through AWS and Dell deployments.
markets: Founded in San Francisco; European operations counted by funding.tech.eu; sells to enterprises via AWS first-party offering and Dell.
rationale: Competes with Cognition and Cursor in enterprise coding AI, where rivals already use F1 to reach engineering-led buyers.

name: Surge AI
desc: Provides data annotation and human-feedback training data to AI labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta.
capacity_detail: Reported revenue USD 1.2 billion in 2024; never raised outside investment; founder Edwin Chen holds 75%
markets: Serves leading AI labs and technology companies plus the US Army, sourcing annotators through platforms such as Data Annotation.
rationale: Highly profitable bootstrapped data supplier with low brand awareness; F1 hospitality could reach AI lab and enterprise buyers.

name: Speak
desc: AI-powered language-learning app offering spoken practice lessons for consumers and businesses through Speak for Business.
capacity_detail: USD 78M Series C at a USD 1B valuation (Dec 2024); USD 162M raised in total
markets: Consumer app strong in Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan, expanding to many more countries; over 200 business customers.
rationale: Consumer subscription brand expanding across Asia and beyond; F1's young international audience suits language learners and paid acquisition.

name: Invisible Technologies
desc: Enterprise AI software platform that structures data, deploys agents and supplies human experts for AI model training.
capacity_detail: USD 100M growth round (Sep 2025) reported by Bloomberg as valuing the company at over USD 2 billion; revenue USD 134M in 2024
sponsorships: Charlotte Hornets listed as a customer (not a sponsorship)
markets: Offices in New York, San Francisco, Washington DC and London; expanding in EMEA; customers include Microsoft and SAIC.
rationale: Scale AI rival seeking enterprise buyers; F1 B2B hospitality and data storytelling fit its enterprise AI positioning.

name: SAS Institute
desc: Privately held analytics and AI software company whose Viya platform serves banks, insurers, healthcare and government customers.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.2 billion in 2022; over USD 3 billion in 2023
markets: Customers in 145 countries; revenue split across Americas, Europe-Middle East-Africa and Asia-Pacific; expanding in China.
rationale: Large analytics vendor preparing a possible IPO; F1's data-driven story suits SAS AI branding against rivals like Alteryx and Snowflake.

name: Zendesk
desc: Customer service software company selling AI agents, ticketing and voice tools; owned by Hellman & Friedman and Permira.
capacity_detail: About USD 500 million annual revenue by 2018 (last public figures before the USD 10.2B take-private in 2022)
markets: Founded in Copenhagen; offices in the US, Ireland, Denmark, UK, Australia and Singapore; customers worldwide.
rationale: Competes with Salesforce, ServiceNow and Genesys, all F1 partners; F1 could showcase its AI agents to global enterprise buyers.

name: Peregrine Technologies
industry: AI data platform for public safety
desc: Data integration and AI platform used by police, emergency services and local governments to connect operational data.
capacity_detail: USD 250M Series D at a USD 6.8 billion valuation (Jun 2026)
markets: Public-safety and government customers in the United States and Canada, with a UK site; also enterprise users.

signals.raise: USD 250M Series D at USD 6.8B valuation (Jun 2026; https://www.crescendo.ai/news/latest-vc-investment-deals-in-ai-startups)

rationale: Palantir-style rival growing fast with fresh capital; F1 offers enterprise and government hospitality, though its public-sector focus limits fit.

name: PixVerse
desc: AI video generation platform offering text- and image-to-video, editing, lip sync and an API to creators.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 2 billion (Jul 2026), Wikipedia list of unicorn startup companies
markets: Consumer and creator platform serving users in more than 177 countries, plus developer API and CLI.
rationale: Consumer creative app competing with Runway and Kling for global creators; F1 content partnerships could showcase AI video generation.

name: Wabi
desc: Consumer AI assistant app for group chats and shared planning, founded by Replika creator Eugenia Kuyda.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 1.25 billion (Oct 2026), Wikipedia list of unicorn startup companies
markets: Consumer app on iOS, Android and desktop; markets not stated.
rationale: Young consumer social app needing mass awareness; F1 fan engagement around group trips and race weekends could suit it.

name: 01.AI
industry: large language model and enterprise AI
desc: Beijing AI company founded by Kai-Fu Lee, known for Yi models, now selling tailored enterprise AI solutions.
capacity_detail: Obtained a valuation over USD 1 billion in November 2023
markets: Primarily China; open-source Yi models distributed internationally; backers include Alibaba Group and Xiaomi.
rationale: Pivoted from pre-training to enterprise solutions; limited international ambitions make an F1 partnership unlikely in the near term.

name: Fireflies.ai
desc: AI meeting notetaker and assistant that records, transcribes and summarises conversations for organisations and individual users.
capacity_detail: Valuation of over USD 1 billion reached after its first tender offer (Jun 2025); profitable since 2023
markets: About 20 million users across more than 500,000 organisations; remote-first team in over 20 countries.
rationale: Profitable fast-growing productivity brand competing with Otter and Zoom; F1 reaches the business professionals who use meeting tools.

name: Sand.ai
desc: Chinese developer of open-source AI video generation models such as MAGI-2 and the VidMuse video creation app.
capacity_detail: USD 200M Series A+ (Nov 2026) at a valuation above USD 1 billion; roughly USD 300M raised to date
markets: China-based; new funds earmarked for international expansion, target markets not named.
rationale: Newly funded video-AI player planning international expansion; F1's Chinese Grand Prix and global audience could support a consumer launch.

name: doubleAI
desc: Israeli AI company led by Amnon Shashua building code execution models that speed up software on CPUs and GPUs.
capacity_detail: USD 200M Series A (Oct 2026) at a valuation of more than USD 1 billion
markets: Early-access product Maxwell; investors include NVIDIA and Dell Technologies Capital; markets not stated.
rationale: Performance-optimisation pitch suits F1's engineering narrative, but the company is early-stage and pre-scale.

name: Traversal
desc: Builds AI site reliability engineering software that finds root causes of production incidents and automates remediation.
capacity_detail: USD 173M raised in total incl. USD 120M Series B at USD 1B valuation (Nov 2026)
markets: Enterprise users include Nubank, Harvey, DigitalOcean and PepsiCo; supports over 4,000 engineers.

signals.raise: USD 120M Series B at USD 1B valuation (Nov 2026; https://www.unite.ai/traversal-raises-120m-series-b-at-1b-valuation-to-expand-ai-sre/)

rationale: Observability rivals Dynatrace and Splunk sponsor F1; reliability under pressure is a natural race-team story for Traversal.

name: Air Space Intelligence
desc: Builds AI software that manages physical operations in aviation, defence, energy and logistics.
capacity_detail: USD 325M Series C at a USD 3 billion valuation (Oct 2026)
markets: Customers in aviation, defence, energy and logistics; specific countries not stated.

signals.raise: USD 325M Series C at USD 3B valuation (Oct 2026; https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/october-2026-unicorn-board-gains-34-tops-1900-ai-defense/)

rationale: Airline and logistics buyers are heavy F1 sponsors; F1's operations-optimisation story mirrors its flight-planning AI pitch.

name: Daytona
desc: Provides isolated cloud environments where AI agents and generated code can run safely at scale.
capacity_detail: USD 60M Series B at a USD 1 billion valuation (Oct 2026)
markets: Developer and AI-agent platform customers; investors include Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung Next; markets not stated.

signals.raise: USD 60M Series B at USD 1B valuation (Oct 2026; https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/october-2026-unicorn-board-gains-34-tops-1900-ai-defense/)

rationale: Developer-infrastructure peers such as Vercel sponsor F1, but Daytona is young and its budget is small.

name: Vinci
desc: Develops physics-based AI software used by engineering teams for hardware design.
capacity_detail: USD 250M Series B at a USD 1.5 billion valuation (Oct 2026), led by Advent International, Temasek and Xora
markets: Hardware engineering teams; investors include AMD Ventures; markets not stated.

signals.raise: USD 250M Series B at USD 1.5B valuation (Oct 2026; https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/october-2026-unicorn-board-gains-34-tops-1900-ai-defense/)

rationale: Simulation rivals Ansys, Siemens and Hexagon partner with F1 teams; aerodynamic and hardware design is a natural showcase.
